'''Atrisian script''' was a [[Writing/Legends|writing system]] used in [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] originating in [[Atrisia/Legends|Atrisia]].

==History==
The script was standardized by the [[First Atrisian Emperor]]. His 53rd successor, [[Uueg Tching]], conquered the whole planet, and established it planetwide.<ref name="WW">{{Hyperspace|url=hyperspace/source/writtenword/index.html?page=1|text=The Written Word|int=The Written Word}}</ref> Atrisian scribes wrote in that script the ''[[Sayings]]'' of [[Uueg Tching]] who taught his heirs, and Uueg intended them to be a guide to his descendants.<ref name="FFCA">{{JournalCite|14|From the Files of Corellia Antilles}}</ref> The script was simplified by [[Eoaq the Expansive]], concurrently with [[Eoaq reforms|his reforms]].<ref name="WW" />

At the time of the [[Cold War (Galactic Republic–Sith Empire)|Cold War]], many inscriptions and advertisements in Atrisian script could be spotted, notably on [[Nar Shaddaa/Legends|Nar Shaddaa]]. This means this script was already in wide galactic use as of [[3653 BBY]].<ref name="TOR">''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]''</ref>

The script gained more popularity in the wider galaxy since [[539 BBY]]<ref>{{JournalCite|14|From the Files of Corellia Antilles}}</ref> when the [[Atrisian Parliament]] made the ''Sayings'' publicly available. The [[Director/Legends|Director]] of the [[Special Acquisitions Branch]] of the [[Library of the Republic]] [[Tra-Skan-Lor]], became a devotee of the ''Sayings'' and enforced it among his personnel, making it part of the Branch's culture. Familiar with the Artisian script, the personnel used the script as an informal in-house cipher.<ref name="WW" />

This usage (as well as appreciation to Tching) continued after the Branch was absorbed into the [[Imperial Intelligence/Legends|Intelligence]] and was even formalized. By the time of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], it was most commonly used for confidential information. [[Computer monitor/Legends|computer monitors]] used by Intelligence staff on the [[Death Star/Legends|Death Stars]] displayed this format.<ref name="screen">[[Star Wars Screen Entertainment|''Star Wars'' Screen Entertainment]]</ref><ref name="WW" /> Another example was the Intelligence detention center on Orinackra.<ref name="WW" /><ref name="DF" />
[[file:codelock.png|thumb|A code lock on Orinackra.]]
An extensive use was on [[code lock]]s in Intelligence installations where one entered a combination using letters from the Atrisian alphabet to access some sections; it was [[Imperial officer/Legends|Officers]] who typically carried [[code key]]s each inscribed with a 3-letter combination. Imperial installations that used Atrisian codes were the [[Weapons Research Facility]] on [[Fest/Legends|Fest]] and the [[Imperial Detention Center]] on [[Orinackra]]. Some [[Cargo container/Legends|crates]] stored in [[Ramsees Hed]] had labels with Atrisian characters.<ref name="DF">''[[Star Wars: Dark Forces]]''</ref>

As a response, [[Alliance Special Operations/Legends|Alliance SpecOps]] personnel frequently used Atrisian to create and transmit tightly-coded, spurious mission plans for the purpose of tying up the resources of Imperial Intelligence, a practice known as "[[salting the ether]]". SpecOps [[General/Legends|General]] [[Crix Masst]], wrote his personal journal in this script.<ref name="WW" />

[[Retro-Paxist poets|Retro-Paxist]] [[Poet/Legends|poet]] [[Horalax]] composed in Atrisian script to help highlight the ironic contrast between the Empire and the empires of the past.<ref name="WW" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|The Atrisian script is meant to represent the typography seen in many LucasArts games, such as ''X-wing'' and the first ''Dark Forces''. Unbeknownst to me, this script apparently has origins in ''Return of the Jedi'', as the image provided with the article demonstrates; this just shows that, even after doing hours of extensive research, an author can miss some very important details!|John Hazlett|<ref name="blog">{{Blog|JSarek|8|Endnotes for The Written Word}}</ref>}}
[[File:Atrisianalphabet.png|thumb|The 12 symbols forming the combinations in the ''X-Wing'' and ''TIE Fighter'' manuals. The 8 characters of the top row appear also in ''Dark Forces'' and are displayed in the picture following the order in which they rotate on the code lock screens. The remaining four are given here in random order.]]
The first appearance of Atrisian characters was probably the copy protection of the original floppy-disk version of [[Star Wars: X-Wing (video game)|''Star Wars: X-Wing'']]. Each page of the "Starfighter Pilot Manual" found in the game box, had a combination of three such characters, along with a name of a galactic location. Each time the player booted the game, a code was given at the registration screen, which the player had to match with one seen in the manual and give the correct password.<ref name="xw">[[Star Wars: X-Wing (video game)|''Star Wars: X-Wing'']], and "Starfighter Pilot Manual"</ref> The symbols were apparently inspired by characters seen on monitor screens in ''[[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|Return of the Jedi]]'',<ref name="blog" /> independently of the [[Aurebesh/Legends|Aurebesh]], which would develop a year later.<ref>{{WebCite|url=http://www.echostation.com/features/aurebesh.htm|text=Aurebesh Soup: ''Recipe for a Star Wars Font Phenomenon''|author=[[Stephen Crane]]|date=2000-10-21|work=Echo Station|language=English|quote=The evolution of the Star Wars alphabet told by the guy who designed the font for West End Games.|archivedate=20160520153232}}</ref> The same tactic was followed later in its spin-off, ''[[Star Wars: TIE Fighter]]''; the combinations here corresponded to [[Star Destroyer/Legends|Star Destroyer]] names or words related to the Empire.<ref name="tie">''[[Star Wars: TIE Fighter]]'', and "Starfighter Pilot Manual"</ref> In both games, all the different combinations were composed of up to 12 different characters.<ref name="tie" /><ref name="xw" /><ref name="erik">{{WebCite|url=https://www.erikstormtrooper.com/darkkatarn.htm|text=Dark Katarn Font|work=Erikstormtrooper's Imperial Gallery|archivedate=20250528025005}}</ref> However the copy protection with the registering sequence, along with the codes, were removed from the "Collector's CD-ROM" releases of [[Star Wars: X-Wing Collector's CD-ROM|both]] [[Star Wars: TIE Fighter Collector's CD-ROM|games]].<ref>''[[Star Wars: X-Wing Collector's CD-ROM]]''</ref><ref>''[[Star Wars: TIE Fighter Collector's CD-ROM]]''</ref>
[[File:Imperial_clock_screensaver.jpg|thumb|The "Imperial Clock" screensaver in ''Star Wars Screen Entertainment'']]
An ornate version of this alphabet appeared in 1994's ''[[Star Wars Screen Entertainment]]'', in a module that was a re-creation of the [[Death Star/Legends|Death Star]] Viewport. Four Atrisian characters are randomly alternating above a planet's schematic.<ref name="screen" /><ref>{{YouTube|channel=@Padawanmage71|name=Padawanmage71|video=r876x9DQk8c|text=Star Wars Screen Entertainment - [07/14] 'Imperial Clock'}}</ref><ref name="erik" />

In ''[[Star Wars: Dark Forces]]'', eight of the symbols that appeared in ''X-Wing'' and ''TIE Fighter'' copy protection, form codes that must be found by the player/[[Kyle Katarn]] and entered in a console in order to access other sections of a level, specifically in Missions 4 and 6. The codes again are composed of three different characters, and must be entered by rotating a series of characters in 3 monitors, thus showing some kind of "alphabetic" order. The Detention Center also shows different numerals on each level, possibly an example of Atrisian numerals. Symbols similar to Atrisian can be also seen on cargo containers, posters and graffiti around some Missions.<ref name="DF" /><ref name="erik" />
<gallery mode=packed caption="Orinackra numerals" widths="80px">

The name of the Atrisian script originated in the essay "[[From the Files of Corellia Antilles]]," published in [[Star Wars Adventure Journal 14|''Star Wars Adventure Journal'' 14]] ([[1997]]) giving the history of the Atrisian Empire.

[[John Hazlett]] attempted to explore the script that appeared in these games and the ''Screen Entertainment'' in the [[2010]] [[Hyperspace: The Official Star Wars Fan Club|Hyperspace]]-exclusive article ''[[The Written Word]]''. Hazlett drew a connection between these symbols (referencing the script's use in ''Dark Forces'' directly, as well as its use in a reproduction of a monitor on the Death Star in ''Screen Entertainment'') with the Imperial Intelligence, and ultimately the Atrisian Empire. In the evolution of the script itself, Hazlett drew historical parallels with [[Wikipedia:Peter I of Russia|Peter the Great's]] reform of the [[Wikipedia:Cyrillic alphabet|Cyrillic alphabet]]. The "Eoaq reforms" attempt to explain the difference between the characters seen in the games, and the cursive writing originally identified as Atrisian script in "From the Files of Corellia Antilles". The editor of the article added a screenshot from ''[[Return of the Jedi]]'' showing a Death Star console where similar characters appear, something that Hazlett admitted he ignored, and confirming that the characters originated in the movies. <ref name="blog" />
